label: GO after an unrewarded rare a2 trial (a2 -> S1, no reward), early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at GO, never at D1 or D2, and never when the previous trial was rewarded. All of its mass is on steps where the model picks a2 (model_act==2, choice logit strongly negative). Its main trigger is the previous trial being a2 -> S1 rare and unrewarded: prev_common==0 has 3.5x lift and 80% of mass, and prev a2 common unrewarded contributes almost nothing. This is the model-based case for staying with a2. It also depends on time in the episode: it fires mostly in trials 0-59 and fades to zero by trial 90, so ep_trial<60 lifts dev precision from 0.59 to 0.92. Magnitude grows over runs of consecutive rare-unrewarded a2 trials (top windows climb 0.6 -> 0.8 -> 0.9 -> 1.0) and is higher when S2 is the good state. Most misses are GO steps on the window first trial, where prev_* is unknown in the window (about 19% of mass at rel -3). Adding those unknown-history cases plus action==2 gives dev F1 0.84 and mass recall 0.96, but that is a window artifact, so I recorded the clean predicate, which uses only observed variables (dev F1 0.81).

issues: The claims hold up. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps) and never when prev_reward==1 (0 of 740k steps). 22185 of its 22209 active steps have action==2.

The rare-transition claim holds. Previous trial a2 common and unrewarded: precision 0.0002, mass recall about 0. Previous trial a1 rare and unrewarded: precision 0. Within the base predicate, high-magnitude cases with good==1 are few (737 predicted steps).

The time dependence is real. Precision of the base predicate by ep_trial range: 0.99 (<10), 0.995 (10-29), 0.97 (30-49), 0.67 (50-59), 0.23 (60-69), 0.16 (70-79), 0.05 (80-89), 0.0 (>=90). This drop is not explained by good state or model_act.

The misses on test are almost all one class: GO steps at rel -3, where prev_* is not in the window (about 19.9% of activation mass). This is a window artifact. No observed-only predicate recovers it cleanly: (rel==-3)&(action==2)&(prev_reward==0)&(ep_trial<60) has precision 0.48.

There is a minor secondary class: GO after an a1 common unrewarded trial (the model switches to a2). It accounts for about 4% of active steps and 1.4% of mass on test, with precision 0.035. This is small noise, not a systematic gap.
The false positives on test (1316 steps) are scattered: they are prev a2 rare unrewarded GO steps where the feature simply did not fire. No separable class stands out.
Test F1 is 0.799 (precision 0.922, recall 0.705, mass recall 0.76), matching the reported scores. The shortfall in recall comes from the window artifact, not from a wrong explanation.
